facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Repealed from 1 January 2004, it had a defined-benefit (DB) pension of half the Last Pay Drawn (LPD) at the time of retirement along with components like Dearness Allowances (DA) etc.
facts.text: The Old Pension Scheme, which guaranteed a defined-benefit pension equal to 50 percent of the last pay drawn, was abolished for new central government entrants starting 1 January 2004.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: The employee contribution shall remain un-altered at 10% of (basic pay + DA).
facts.text: Under the National Pension System and the Unified Pension Scheme, employees contribute a mandatory deduction of 10 percent of basic pay and dearness allowance from their monthly salary.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Enhancement of the mandatory contribution by the Central Government for its employees covered under NPS Tier-I from the existing 10% to 14%.
facts.text: The central government raised its mandatory employer contribution under NPS Tier-I from 10 percent to 14 percent of basic pay plus dearness allowance.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: The Government contribution will increase from the present 14% to 18.5%.
facts.text: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the government contribution increases from 14 percent to 18.5 percent of basic pay and dearness allowance.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Assured pension: 50% of the average basic pay drawn over the last 12 months prior to superannuation for a minimum qualifying service of 25 years.
facts.text: The Unified Pension Scheme guarantees an assured pension payout of 50 percent of average basic pay drawn over the last 12 months prior to superannuation for at least 25 years of service.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Assured minimum pension: @10,000 per month on superannuation after minimum 10 years of service.
facts.text: A minimum assured pension of 10,000 rupees per month is guaranteed under the Unified Pension Scheme upon superannuation after at least 10 years of service.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Contributions made towards NPS are eligible for an additional tax deduction under section 80CCD(1B) upto Rs. 50,000 which is over and above the Rs 1,50,000 limit of deduction available under sec 80CCD(1).
facts.text: Salaried taxpayers contributing to the National Pension System can claim an additional income tax deduction of up to 50,000 rupees under Section 80CCD(1B).

facts.label: official
facts.quote: In the Union Budget 2019, the tax exemption limit for lumpsum withdrawal on exit/maturity from NPS has been increased from the present 40% to 60% under section 10(12A) of the IT Act and the remaining 40% of the corpus is already tax-exempt as it is mandatorily utilized for annuity purchase.
facts.text: Subscribers exiting the National Pension System at retirement are eligible to withdraw up to 60 percent of their accumulated corpus completely tax-free.
